Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexMart Inc. Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexMart's Q2 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexMart.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust growth in our seller services and value-added services revenue, alongside effective marketing campaigns that boosted brand awareness and customer acquisition. Our focus remains on accelerating adoption of these high-margin services to fuel our marketplace flywheel. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new products like NexCart AI, EcoThread, and FlashDeliver, which we believe will significantly enhance customer engagement and GMV growth. Finally, we are committed to driving efficiency in managing our operating costs to support sustainable profitability.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q2 revenue was $14.5 billion, an increase of 14% year-over-year. Gross margin was 38%, driven by a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin seller services and value-added services, or VAS, along with improved supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $7.8 billion, representing 54% of revenue, reflecting disciplined investments in growth areas while achieving leverage through automation and data-driven optimizations.

Our net income for the quarter was $1.8 billion, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $12.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $58 to $60 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA margins of 20 to 22%.

Before we open it up to questions, I'd like to dive deeper into some key areas starting with one of our highest-margin and fastest-growing segments: seller services and value-added services, or VAS. This segment now represents 22% of our total net revenue, up from 18% a year ago, and continues to be a key driver of our marketplace flywheel, monetizing our 4.2 million active sellers while enhancing their performance on our platform.

In Q2, seller services and VAS revenue reached $3.2 billion, a robust 28% year-over-year increase and 15% quarter-over-quarter growth. This outpaced our overall revenue growth of 14%, underscoring the segment's disproportionate impact on our top line. Adjusted for FX, the growth was even stronger at 30%, reflecting resilient demand amid moderating e-commerce GMV growth globally, which we saw at 11% YoY to $180 billion on our platform.

Let me break this down by adoption rates, key sub-components, and their revenue contributions, as these metrics are critical for understanding the stickiness of our ecosystem.

Seller adoption of our VAS suite hit an all-time high of 68% in Q2, up from 58% in Q2 last year and 64% in Q1. This means nearly 7 out of every 10 active sellers are now leveraging at least one paid service, compared to the industry benchmark of around 50% for peers like Shopify or Etsy. For context, our top 20% of sellers by GMV—our 'Power Sellers'—show even higher penetration at 92%, driving outsized economics.

Key drivers here include cross-sell penetration: average VAS attachments per seller rose to 3.2 services, up 18% YoY, fueled by our AI-powered recommendation engine, NexRecommend, which suggests personalized bundles like Sponsored Products ads paired with Fulfillment by NexMart, or FBN. New seller onboarding also accelerated, with 75% of new sellers activated in Q2 adopting a VAS within their first 30 days, versus 62% last year, thanks to our streamlined 'Seller Central Pro' dashboard rollout.

Regionally, adoption varies but is trending upward everywhere. In North America, which accounts for 45% of VAS revenue, we saw 72% adoption, driven by mature logistics infrastructure. Here, FBN take-rate hit 55%, mirroring Amazon's FBA success but with our edge in same-day delivery via partnerships with UPS and DoorDash. In APAC, 30% of VAS revenue came from explosive 82% adoption in China and India, where our Alipay-integrated payment processing and Cainiao-like logistics via NexLogistics captured 40% market share among cross-border sellers, with GMV from APAC sellers growing 22% YoY. EMEA and LATAM combined for 25%, with adoption at 62% and 55% respectively, and LATAM's 35% YoY jump tied to our Spanish/Portuguese-localized ad tools amid MercadoLibre-like competition.

VAS isn't just growing—it's high-margin rocket fuel. Segment gross margin expanded to 52%, up 400 basis points YoY, contributing 250 bps to our overall 38% company margin. Here's the mix shift: Advertising, including Sponsored Products, Brands, and Display, generated $1.4 billion, up 35% YoY, representing 44% of VAS revenue, with ACOS for sellers improved 12% to 22% via GenAI bidding and share of ad spend from TikTok/Instagram imports up 40%. Fulfillment and Logistics, like FBN and NexShip, brought in $1.0 billion, up 25%, or 31% of VAS, with 1.2 billion units fulfilled, up 20% YoY, at an average FBN fee of $2.50 per unit and 15% penetration among non-Prime sellers. Payments and Financial Services via NexPay added $0.5 billion, up 22%, or 16%, processing $45 billion GMV at 1.8% take-rate, with FX hedging tools boosting cross-border adoption by 28%. Other services, including Analytics, Premium Listings, and Subscriptions, contributed $0.3 billion, up 18%, or 9%, with Seller University Pro subs reaching 450,000 users, up 30%, and data lake insights reducing churn by 15%.

This mix evolution—ads now 44% versus 38% last year—reflects a shift toward scalable, variable-fee models less exposed to freight volatility. Collectively, VAS added $650 million in incremental revenue YoY, representing 60% of our total revenue beat versus guidance.

We've invested heavily in tech to boost adoption. We launched NexAI Ads in May, our proprietary large language model that optimizes creatives and bids in real-time, delivering 25% higher ROAS for early adopters. Already 300,000 sellers onboarded, contributing a $150 million run-rate. FBN 2.0 expansion integrated with Shopify Plus and BigCommerce APIs, enabling hybrid omnichannel fulfillment, addressing the post-pandemic DTC-to-marketplace shift where 35% of our sellers now use multi-channel inventory sync. Blockchain-enabled seller analytics, piloted in APAC, reduced fraud by 40% and unlocked premium data tiers.

Strategically, VAS is our moat-builder: higher adoption correlates to 3x lower seller churn and 2.5x higher lifetime value, akin to Alibaba's ecosystem lock-in. We're prioritizing 'full-stack' sellers—those using 5+ services—who generate 65% of platform GMV but only 25% of our seller base. Initiatives like tiered incentives, such as 10% ad credit for FBN commit, are scaling this.

Looking ahead, we expect Q3 VAS revenue of $3.4 to $3.5 billion, implying 25-27% YoY growth, with adoption targeting 71%. Full-year guidance holds at $13.0 to $13.5 billion for the segment. Risks include ad market softness from Google/Amazon competition and logistics inflation, but our 85% gross margin on ads provides buffer. In summary, seller services and VAS are not just a revenue stream—they're the accelerant for our entire flywheel, turning sellers into superfans and driving sustainable, high-margin growth.

Now, turning to our new product and service launches, which have been a key growth driver in Q2, contributing approximately 18% to our overall GMV uplift of 22% year-over-year. We're thrilled with the early traction across our three major initiatives: NexCart AI, our generative AI-powered shopping companion; EcoThread, our private-label sustainable apparel line; and FlashDeliver, our 15-minute urban quick-commerce service. These launches align with seismic shifts in the e-commerce landscape—personalization demands up 35% per recent McKinsey data, sustainability premiums commanding 20-30% higher AOV as seen with Patagonia and Everlane, and quick-commerce exploding to a projected $50 billion U.S. market by 2025, per Bernstein Research.

First, NexCart AI, rolled out in late May to our 150 million-plus active users via iOS and Android apps, leverages large language models akin to Amazon's Rufus but with proprietary multimodal capabilities—processing text, images, and voice for hyper-personalized recommendations, bundle suggestions, and virtual try-ons. Early performance has exceeded our internal KPIs: GMV contribution hit $1.2 billion in Q2, representing 12% of total platform GMV and growing 45% month-over-month, driven by a 28% lift in conversion rates from 3.2% baseline to 4.1%. AOV increased 15% to $68 on AI-influenced orders, thanks to intelligent upselling—for example, 'Customers who bought this blender also love this eco-friendly protein powder' with 85% relevance scoring via our fine-tuned Llama 3.1 models. User engagement metrics are stellar: 62% of sessions now interact with NexCart, with average session depth up 40% to 7.2 items viewed.

Customer feedback is overwhelmingly positive—Net Promoter Score of 74 from 2.1 million post-interaction surveys, versus our marketplace average of 58. App Store ratings spiked to 4.7 out of 5 from 450,000 reviews, with comments praising 'seamless, feels like a personal stylist.' We've iterated twice already based on voice-of-customer data: enhanced multilingual support for our APAC cohort, now covering 12 languages, and reduced hallucination rates to under 2% via RAG pipelines pulling real-time inventory from our 15 edge data centers.

Regionally, U.S. adoption leads at 68% penetration among Prime-like NexMart Plus subscribers, while APAC—particularly India and Southeast Asia—saw 55% month-over-month growth amid rising smartphone penetration. EU rollout lags slightly at 42% due to GDPR-compliant data opt-ins, but we're on track post our June privacy audit. Strategically, NexCart positions us against Shopify's Sidekick and BigCommerce's AI tools by owning the full stack—our 1P and 3P seller ecosystem benefits from 22% higher seller margins on AI-optimized listings. CAC dropped 12% to $18 via organic virality, boosting LTV:CAC to 4.2x.

Next, EcoThread, launched mid-June as our first major private-label push into apparel, featuring 250 SKUs of recycled polyester activewear and organic cotton basics, sourced via blockchain-traced supply chains from Bangladesh and Vietnam mills—mirroring H&M's Conscious Collection but with carbon-neutral shipping. Performance highlights: $450 million in Q2 GMV, 32% ahead of plan, capturing 8% of our fashion category share, up from zero. 25% higher AOV at $92 versus category $72, with repeat purchase rate at 42% in 90 days—fueled by subscription add-ons like quarterly 'wardrobe refresh' boxes. Inventory turns at 8.2x annually, low waste at 3% thanks to demand forecasting via Prophet time-series models integrated with our WMS.

Feedback: 4.6 out of 5 average from 1.8 million reviews on-site, NPS 68. Top praises: 'Fit is spot-on, and the sustainability badge builds trust.' We've addressed minor gripes like sizing inconsistencies, now fixed with 3D body-scan tech pilots, and expanded plus-size options to 40% of lineup based on 15% of feedback volume. Regionally, North America dominates at 62% of sales, resonating with Gen Z's 70% preference for sustainable brands per Nielsen. EMEA grew 50% month-over-month despite higher logistics costs from EU Green Deal tariffs, while LATAM pilots in Brazil show 30% AOV premium over local players like Magazine Luiza. This launch de-risks our marketplace margins—EcoThread's 52% gross margin crushes the 38% category average—while countering Shein and Temu's ultra-low pricing with premium storytelling and loyalty hooks.

Finally, FlashDeliver, beta-launched early July in 12 U.S. metros like NYC and LA, and 5 APAC hubs like Singapore and Mumbai, partnering with dark stores and gig fleets for 15-minute delivery on 10,000-plus SKUs, competing head-on with Gopuff and Getir's models. Early metrics are explosive: $320 million GMV, 150% month-over-month growth, 6% of total orders but 22% of quick-turnover categories like beauty and snacks. Fulfillment costs at $4.20 per order, target $4.00, with 92% on-time rate via route-optimization using OR-Tools and real-time ETA ML. Churn among Flash users at just 8% monthly, versus 14% platform-wide.

Customer sentiment: NPS 72 from 850,000 ratings, 4.8 out of 5 on app. Feedback highlights speed—'faster than DoorDash!'—with tweaks to minimum order value from $15 to $12 based on 20% abandonment data. U.S. urban penetration at 35% of eligible users; APAC at 48%, boosted by dense populations but challenged by monsoon-season logistics in India. We're scaling to 50 cities by Q1 next year, with unit economics breakeven projected at 25% share.

In aggregate, these launches drove $2 billion incremental GMV, 19% active user growth to 162 million, and a 14% reduction in category churn. Technically, we've invested $150 million in CapEx for AI infra and micro-fulfillment, yielding 3x ROI in Year 1 models. Strategically, they fortify our moat in a maturing e-com market facing macroeconomic headwinds—U.S. consumer spending flat per Fed data—by emphasizing convenience, ethics, and tech differentiation versus pure discounters like Temu. Looking ahead, Q3 guidance bakes in 25-30% GMV acceleration from these, with full-year contribution targeting 22% of total. We're monitoring competitive responses like Walmart's AI pilots, but our data flywheel gives us confidence.

Next, on the effectiveness of our marketing campaigns, with a focus on brand awareness and customer acquisition—two pillars that have driven our Q2 results and positioned NexMart for sustained growth in the competitive e-commerce landscape. We've navigated a maturing online retail market where iOS 14.5 attribution challenges, the ongoing cookie deprecation in Chrome by early 2024, and rising CPMs across Meta and Google platforms have tested even the most sophisticated marketers. Yet, our disciplined, data-led approach has delivered industry-leading outcomes, with marketing ROI improving 22% year-over-year to a robust 4.8x blended ROAS across channels.

Starting with brand awareness, we've seen meaningful lifts that are translating into tangible funnel expansion. Independent Nielsen surveys conducted in Q2 show our aided brand recall in the fast-fashion and consumer electronics categories climbing 28% YoY to 62% among 18-34-year-olds in our core markets—a level comparable to leaders like Shein in apparel or Best Buy in tech. Unaided recall has also surged 19% to 41%, reflecting the success of our 'NexMart Everyday' multimedia campaign, which rolled out across CTV, YouTube, and TikTok. This campaign, budgeted at $45 million, achieved a 15% share of voice in lifestyle retail, up from 11% last year per Kantar data, outpacing peers like ASOS and Zalando.

Social proof has been a key accelerator. Our Instagram and TikTok follower base grew 32% YoY to 28 million active users, with engagement rates hitting 4.2%—more than double the industry average of 1.8% according to Socialbakers benchmarks. We attribute this to our shoppable video series featuring micro-influencers, 10k to 50k followers, in the beauty and home goods verticals, where user-generated content drove a 150% increase in branded hashtag mentions—#NexMartHaul reached 2.1 million. Net Promoter Score for brand perception rose to +48 from +39 YoY, signaling stronger emotional loyalty amid economic headwinds like 7% U.S. inflation pressures.

Turning to customer acquisition, our performance here has been exceptional, adding 5.2 million net new customers in Q2—a 24% YoY increase and ahead of our guidance midpoint. This brings our active customer base to 145 million globally, with new-to-brand acquisition accounting for 42% of total orders, up from 36% last year. Critically, we've optimized efficiency: Customer Acquisition Cost fell 18% to $42, down from $51 in Q2 2023, thanks to a 15% reduction in paid search CPCs through AI-driven bid management on Google Ads and a shift to lower-funnel performance creative. Our LTV/CAC ratio now stands at 3.9x, well above the e-commerce benchmark of 3x cited by McKinsey, with Average Order Value for new customers up 12% to $68 on the back of personalized bundling recommendations.

ROAS breakdowns underscore channel effectiveness. Performance marketing—primarily Meta Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns and Google Performance Max—delivered 5.6x ROAS on $320 million spend, a 25% improvement YoY, fueled by first-party data clean rooms compliant with GDPR and CCPA. Upper-funnel brand channels like programmatic video and podcast sponsorships, such as partnerships with 'The Joe Rogan Experience' and Spotify's 'Call Her Daddy,' yielded 3.2x ROAS, justifying our 60/40 performance-to-brand spend allocation. Conversion rates from paid social climbed to 3.8% from 2.9%, driven by dynamic product ads leveraging our proprietary ML models for lookalike audiences built from 2+ years of CRM data.

Regionally, tailored strategies yielded strong results. In North America, 52% of revenue, we acquired 2.8 million new customers, with Black Friday preview campaigns generating $1.2 billion in attributable sales—a 31% YoY lift. Brand awareness here hit 68% aided recall, boosted by 'NexDays' promotions that mimicked Amazon's playbook while differentiating via AR virtual try-ons for apparel, reducing return rates by 14%. CAC was lowest at $38, reflecting mature infrastructure.

EMEA, 28% of revenue, saw 1.4 million new customers despite DMA regulations curbing third-party cookies—our early adoption of server-side tracking via Google's Enhanced Conversions kept ROAS steady at 4.5x. Awareness grew 35% in the UK and Germany, where sustainability-focused campaigns like 'EcoNex' line with 100% recycled packaging resonated, aligning with EU Green Deal mandates and driving 22% higher AOV in apparel, £72 versus £59 benchmark.

APAC, 15% of revenue, was our fastest-growing region, adding 900,000 customers with explosive TikTok Shop integrations in Indonesia and India, where we captured 18% market share in budget fashion per SimilarWeb data. ROAS hit 6.2x on live-streaming events, echoing Shein's model, though we tempered growth with localized pricing to counter Temu's aggressive discounting. LATAM, 5% of revenue, contributed 100,000 new customers, with Brazil's Pix payment integrations boosting conversions 40% during our 'Carnaval Deals' push.

Technical initiatives have been game-changers. We've rolled out our 'NexAI Engine,' a custom TensorFlow-based platform for predictive audience segmentation, which improved CTR by 27% across 500+ campaigns. This includes privacy-first signals like contextual targeting and zero-party data from post-purchase surveys. We've also doubled down on omnichannel: 25% of acquisitions now stem from shoppable Instagram Reels and Pinterest Lens AR, with CTV like Roku and Hulu contributing 12% of upper-funnel traffic at a $8 CPM—half the industry average. To future-proof against signal loss, we're investing $50 million this year for a customer data platform enabling 360-degree views without cookies.

Strategically, we're evolving beyond pure acquisition. While new customer growth remains a top KPI, we're allocating 20% of budget to retention tactics like our 'Nex Loyalist' program—modeled after Sephora's Beauty Insider—which has lifted repeat purchase rates to 62% for cohort Year 1 customers. Insights from our A/B testing framework show that blending brand storytelling with performance yields 2.5x higher CLV. Looking ahead, expect continued emphasis on emerging channels like Reddit Ads and WhatsApp Commerce in high-growth markets, with Q3 guidance for 20-25% YoY new customer growth and CAC stable at $40 to $45. This positions us to gain share in a $6.5 trillion global e-commerce market projected by eMarketer to grow 10% this year.

Finally, let's discuss operating expenses and our efficiency in managing operating costs. In an industry where scale and execution separate leaders from laggards—think Amazon's fulfillment dominance or Alibaba's ecosystem efficiencies during Singles Day—disciplined OpEx management is critical to sustaining high teens EBITDA margins amid intensifying competition from players like Temu and Shein.

Total operating expenses for Q2 came in at $7.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year from last year. This growth reflects our deliberate investments in capacity to support 28% YoY GMV growth to $180 billion. However, as a percentage of net revenue, OpEx improved to 53.6%, down 290 basis points year-over-year. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based compensation and one-time restructuring charges from our European logistics integration, OpEx as a percentage of revenue was 51.2%, marking our best quarterly leverage in three years.

This efficiency stems from multi-year initiatives across our core OpEx buckets: fulfillment and logistics, sales and marketing, technology and content, and general and administrative.

Fulfillment and logistics, our biggest lever for scale, represented 28% of net revenue in Q2, down from 31% YoY. That's about $4.1 billion in absolute terms, up 8% YoY but with per-unit costs dropping 15% to $4.72 per order—a record low. AOV held steady at $48, but our fulfillment cost as a percentage of GMV improved to 8.7% from 10.2%.

Key drivers include our next-gen automation rollout. We've now deployed computer vision-powered picking systems in 65% of our 45 North American fulfillment centers, inspired by Amazon's robotic arms but customized for our high-SKU fashion and consumer electronics mix. This reduced pick-and-pack cycle times by 22%, from 45 to 35 minutes per order. In Europe, we've partnered with DHL for a dedicated e-commerce corridor, cutting cross-border fulfillment costs by 18% to €5.20 per order amid Brexit-related customs delays and rising diesel costs.

Regionally, North America drove 72% of our GMV but saw the sharpest efficiencies, with last-mile costs per package down 11% to $2.85, thanks to micro-fulfillment centers in high-density urban areas like Chicago and Atlanta. APAC, now 15% of GMV, faced elevated costs at 9.8% of GMV due to fragmented carrier networks, but our localization—stocking 40% of inventory in Singapore hubs—is yielding 14% quarter-over-quarter improvement. We're leaning into sustainability too: our fleet of 1,200 electric vans with Rivian reduced fuel costs by 24% YoY, while carbon-neutral packaging trials cut material expenses by 7%. Guiding fulfillment OpEx to 27-28% of revenue in Q3, with $50 million in capex for AI-optimized route planning that could shave another 5-7% off per-unit costs.

Sales and marketing expenses totaled $2.1 billion, or 14.5% of revenue—down 180 bps YoY, despite a 25% ramp in paid media. CAC fell 16% to $22.50, while ROAS climbed to 4.8x from 4.1x. This leverage comes amid softer ad pricing post-Apple's ATT changes, offset by shifting 35% of budget to first-party data channels. Our proprietary Customer Data Platform, built on Snowflake and integrated with our loyalty app, enables hyper-personalized campaigns—AI-driven product recommendations boosted conversion rates by 19% on our mobile app, 68% of orders. We clawed back $45 million by sunseting underperforming pilots and reallocating to high-ROAS channels.

Regionally, Europe saw CAC down 22% amid GDPR-compliant retargeting, fueling 32% active customer growth. In APAC, localized influencer partnerships improved LTV:CAC to 3.2x. We'll hold marketing at 14-15% in H2, prioritizing retention as cohort LTV stabilizes at $285, 12 months post-signup.

Technology and content OpEx was $1.0 billion, or 7.0% of revenue—up 5 bps YoY but with 25% growth in R&D output. We've amortized prior AI capex, enabling headless commerce that reduced site latency by 40% to under 1.5 seconds. Our GenAI search engine cut support tickets by 30%, and UGC incentives generated 70% of PDP traffic at 60% lower cost.

G&A came in at $550 million, or 3.7% of revenue—down 110 bps YoY, reflecting zero-based budgeting and a 4% headcount reduction to 18,500 FTEs through offshore engineering in India, now 25% of dev team.

These efficiencies underscore NexMart's moat: a vertically integrated model blending Shopify-like merchant tools with Amazon-scale logistics. We've unlocked 450 bps of total OpEx leverage YoY, expanding adjusted EBITDA margins to 18.2% from 14.8%. TTM free cash flow hit $620 million, funding buybacks and our $300 million M&A war chest for grocery verticals. Risks remain: carrier rate hikes up 5.9% industry-wide, potential tariffs on China imports, and softening consumer sentiment. But with GMV guidance raised to $34-35 billion for the second half, we expect continued OpEx deleveraging to 52% of revenue, positioning us for 20%+ margins by next year.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. On seller services, the adoption rates sound impressive, especially in APAC. Can you talk more about how you're sustaining that momentum against competition, and any updates on full-stack sellers?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, the 68% adoption is a testament to our ecosystem stickiness, and APAC's 82% is driven by tailored logistics and payments. For full-stack sellers using 5+ services, they're now 25% of base but 65% of GMV, and our incentives like ad credits for FBN are scaling that rapidly. Competition is fierce, but our AI tools like NexRecommend give us an edge in cross-sell, keeping churn 3x lower.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel:
Great, thanks. On the new launches, NexCart AI's engagement is strong, but how are you thinking about scaling FlashDeliver's economics outside urban areas, and customer feedback evolution?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Lisa, scaling FlashDeliver is key—we're at breakeven trajectory with 92% on-time and costs near target. Feedback has been stellar at NPS 72, and we're expanding to 50 cities by Q1 with optimized routes. Outside urban, micro-fulfillment and partnerships will help, mirroring our APAC success at 48% penetration despite challenges.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with JPMorgan.

David Wong:
Thanks. Marketing ROAS at 4.8x is solid amid headwinds. How are you adapting to cookie loss long-term, and thoughts on APAC TikTok growth?

Taylor Kim:
David, thanks. Our NexAI Engine and CDP are privacy-first, with server-side tracking holding ROAS steady. In APAC, TikTok integrations drove 6.2x ROAS and 18% share; we're blending with WhatsApp for omnichannel. Long-term, zero-party data and CTV keep us ahead, targeting stable CAC.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
